title: Financial Assistance Policy, Section 6 — Encounters Covered by an Approved Award
content:
**6.1** One approved award under the Financial Assistance Program (Charity Care) covers every eligible encounter of the patient, each booked separately: encounters whose service start date falls between the award start date and the award end date inclusive, whether billed before or after the approval.

**6.2** An encounter is eligible only when all three hold:
- its services are emergency or medically necessary (elective non-covered services are excluded);
- its open balance is the patient's own — a self-pay liability, or the patient-responsibility portion of an insured encounter where insured patient-responsibility balances are eligible;
- its charges are Riverbend's own (the covered providers); charges of the providers practicing at Riverbend whose charges the award does not cover are billed by those groups and are outside the award.

**6.3** Under a medical hardship award, the patient's liabilities across all covered encounters together never exceed the award's hardship liability cap, measured as the sum of the FAP liabilities booked on the case's encounter applications within the award period; once the cap is reached, every later covered encounter carries zero liability.

**6.4** An encounter is applied once per case.

### Points of judgement

| Question | Answer under this section |
|---|---|
| Is an encounter with a service start date equal to the award end date covered? | Yes — both dates are inclusive. |
| Does it matter that the encounter was billed after the approval? | No — billing before or after the approval makes no difference. |
| Can the same encounter be applied twice on one case? | No — once per case. |

Hypothetical illustration of 6.3: under a hardship cap of 1,000.00 USD, encounters already booked with liabilities of 600.00 and 400.00 USD exhaust the cap, and every later covered encounter on that case carries zero liability.
